name: GPT

lifecycle.note: Archived repository; the pretrained weights (params_0.npy to params_9.npy) remain downloadable from OpenAI on GitHub.

sources.locator: page date; first paragraph and Drawbacks

summary.text: GPT is a transformer language model from OpenAI, published in June 2018 with a paper and released with its code and pretrained weights under the MIT licence. It was pre-trained without supervision on BooksCorpus and then fine-tuned on smaller supervised datasets for specific tasks; OpenAI released it so others could skip the costly pre-training step.

contextWindowTokens.note: Training sequence length: the paper trains on contiguous sequences of 512 tokens, the post says sequences of up to 512 tokens.

parameters.note: OpenAI describes the architecture (12-layer decoder-only transformer, 768-dimensional states, 12 attention heads) but gives no parameter count in the GPT materials. The GPT-2 paper calls its 117M model equivalent to the original GPT, and the GPT-2 repository later said that count was wrong, so no figure is recorded.

notes: The June 2018 post and paper do not give the model a name; OpenAI later calls it GPT and the original GPT (GPT-2 announcement and paper), so GPT is used as the name. The slug is gpt-1 because gpt is the family id. Training compute and data (BooksCorpus, over 7,000 unpublished books) are described in the post and paper.
